description_full: Clarivate Plc provides information services in the Americas, the Middle East, Africa, Europe, and the Asia Pacific. It operates through three segments: Academia & Government, Intellectual Property, and Life Sciences & Healthcare. The company offers scientific and academic research solutions; Web of Science Research Intelligence, an AI-native solution; ProQuest solutions to access multidisciplinary curated content, such as databases, dissertations, news, primary sources, books, and video formats; library software, including Alma, library services platform; and Vega and Polaris for public libraries. It also provides patent maintenance and administrative services; Derwent Innovation, an AI-powered search; Derwent World Patents Index to identify related concepts in patent publications and navigate new or unfamiliar technology categories; CompuMark, a trademark search and watch solutions; IP Recordals managed services; and RiskMark, an AI-powered tool for evaluating trademark risk and argument drafting support. In addition, the company offers IPfolio, a management platform; FoundationIP solution for law firms; Cortellis for decisions related to assessing the market, analyzing competitors, regulatory compliance, and drug safety; Regulatory Intelligence platform; commercial solutions; and Medtech solutions. It serves academic institutions, government agencies, and life sciences, and pharmaceutical companies. The company was formerly known as Clarivate Analytics Plc and changed its name to Clarivate Plc in May 2020. Clarivate Plc was founded in 1864 and is headquartered in London, the United Kingdom.

financial_summary: Clarivate Plc is a small-cap technology business with a $1.5B market cap on $2.5B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at -3% over the past three years, and a shrinking top line is the hardest headwind any business can overcome.
Returns on capital run at -3% against a 8% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests.
The business throws off $365M in free cash flow — roughly 15 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders.
On the balance sheet, debt is heavy at 4.8× net debt/EBITDA, and leverage like that is what turns a bad year into a permanent loss, and thin 0.3× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.

Shareholder yield is only 0.0%, a thin return of capital, and insiders hold 18% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and profit capture is only 0.1× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.
